subject: Performance deep-dive: workload velocity & sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@parcelio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Performance deep-dive: workload velocity & sizing follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today, good context. This note captures what we heard and the immediate asks so we can size a pilot and draft an SOW. TL;DR: we think a 4-week pilot with a small dedicated pool + streaming-capable nodes will validate the steady vs peak sizing and latency targets.

Key constraints you mentioned (confirm if any are off):
- Target end-to-end p95 latency: < 150 ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens); p95 streaming chunk latency <= 120 ms.
- Typical steady-state traffic: ~25 QPS average (user-facing inference calls).
- Peak crest: brief bursts up to ~200 QPS (10-15 minute crest windows during some promotional events).
- Concurrency (streaming): up to 25 concurrent streams at peak; pilot can enforce a 20-stream cap.
- Token mix: average response ~320 tokens; bursts can spike to 1,200 tokens per request.
- Business ask: avoid >2% tail errors during peaks; cost target ~reduce token cost by 15% vs current infra baseline.

Immediate follow-ups from our side:
1) Please share a 1-week traffic sample (CSV) with per-request timestamps, token lengths, and a flag for streaming vs non-streaming. We can use aggregated PDFs but prefer raw CSV for sizing.
2) We'll run an initial sizing recommendation (GPU pool & streaming worker mix) and propose a pilot config by EOD Thursday PT.
3) Ops questions below that help sizing: model variant (64B/16B/8B quant), KV cache hit expectations, whether you expect session pinning, and any hard latency hops (external deps) we should factor in.

Attachments: I attached a pilot SOW template and a sample CSV schema.

Next steps (proposed):
- Samir: send traffic sample + confirm pilot cap (20 vs 25 streams) — by Wed EOD PT.
- Redwood (Mina/Marissa): sizing + draft SOW — by Thu EOD PT.
- Schedule pilot kickoff (30–45 min) once SOW is agreed.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: draft-sla-and-sow.pdf (pdf), sample-traffic-schema.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive: workload velocity & sizing follow-up

Mina — quick ops notes to add to the sizing checklist (will drive GPU selection and batching):

- Model variant: ask Parcelio whether they plan to use a 4-bit quantized 13B or a 16B float model for the pilot. 13B-4bit changes memory and KV cache tradeoffs.
- KV cache: if they expect high session locality (repeated user context), prefix caching can reduce token compute by ~25%; request they indicate expected session reuse pct.
- Sequence length distro: we need a percentile breakdown (p50/p90/p99) of input + output token lengths. If p99 output > 1k tokens, we need to size for longer KV lifetimes and more memory.
- Streaming details: confirm whether they plan to use chunked streaming (small chunk sizes) or whole-response streaming — chunked favors lower p95 but increases churn on the runtime.
- Cold start behavior: do they expect many one-off sessions or pinned sessions for conversational flows?

Operational asks (for the CSV): per-request fields: timestamp (ms), request_id, request_tokens, response_tokens, streaming_flag, region, user_type (internal/test/prod). If they can include a small sample with a high-crest window that’s ideal.

I'll draft two candidate configs: (A) small dedicated pool + 2 streaming workers, (B) medium pool with autoscale for crest windows — we can recommend pricing delta and expected p95 under both.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Performance & Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir@parcelio.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Parcelio Platform Team <platform@parcelio.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive: workload velocity & sizing follow-up

Thanks Mina — attaching the 7-day export (parcelio_traffic_sample_apr2027.csv). Highlights from our side:
- Steady-state: 22–28 QPS (most business hours PST).
- Observed short crest on 2027-04-03 11:44–11:58 UTC where QPS peaked at ~210 for ~14 minutes; median response tokens at crest ~460, some outliers up to 1,100 tokens.
- Streaming usage currently ~12% of calls but growing; we expect ~18–20% within 2 months.

Answers to ops items:
- Model: pilot will use 13B quant (4-bit) for cost reasons; we may test a 16B later.
- KV cache: session affinity is high for conversational flows — estimate ~48% reuse across sessions for returning users.
- Streaming: we use chunked streaming (small chunks ~120–160 tokens).
- Cold starts: mostly short-lived sessions; we won't pin sessions for the pilot.

Also flag: procurement is looking for a 12-month committed discount if we sign up for a dedicated pool after pilot — they asked for a ballpark discount range to include in the SOW.

Attachments: parcelio_traffic_sample_apr2027.csv (csv)

Samir

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive: workload velocity & sizing follow-up

Samir — thanks for the sample and the clarifications, that’s exactly what we need. Quick recap and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Sizing recap (initial recommendation):
- Pilot config (Week 1–4): 3 dedicated streaming-capable instances (NVIDIA A10-style equivalent) + 2 standard inference nodes. This maps to expected steady p95 < 120 ms and should absorb the 14-minute crest with autoscale triggers (we’ll simulate the 210 QPS crest in test).
- Expected pilot caps: enforce 20 concurrent streams (you can opt to increase to 25 post-pilot).
- Cost delta: ~+28% above our hosted baseline for dedicated pilot; if Parcelio commits to a 12-month reserved capacity we can outline a 15–25% discount range depending on commit level.

Operational asks (what we’ll do next):
1) Redwood will run a crest simulation based on your CSV and share performance projections + estimated token cost for the pilot by Mon EOD PT.
2) I’ll send a draft SOW (DocuSign link) with the pilot scope and a placeholder discount band for committed capacity. Please review and we’ll adjust.
3) Kickoff: propose Tue 13 Apr 2027 10:00 AM PT for a 30-minute pilot kickoff and test-run. If that works I’ll send an invite.

Samir — if you can confirm pilot kickoff time and whether procurement needs anything else included in the SOW (e.g., specific SLAs or audit clauses), we’ll incorporate.

Thanks — Mina

--
